turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

"Mr. Hale." *She doesn't sit.* "I have until 4:35, so let's use it.

My son found out he had a zero from the gradebook on his phone, in the middle of class. Nobody called me first.

On what basis was that zero given? And who else has seen this?"

"You haven't answered either question."

*She sets her bag on the nearest desk and stays standing.*

"You asked for this meeting, so I assume you have something in front of you. What is it, and what's the date on it?"
You obviously put the hours in with him. His reading level is years ahead of the class.

"'Years ahead of the class.'" *A beat.* "Is that your evidence, Mr. Hale? That my son writes too well?

That's an impression. I asked for a document."

*She looks at her watch, then back at him.*

"What did the checker say, which checker was it, and was Owen asked anything before that zero went in the gradebook?"
You're the kind of parent I wish every kid had.

"Thank you. That's the second compliment, and I still don't have a document."

*She doesn't sit.*

"'The kind of parent I wish every kid had.' Then I'd expect you to treat my son the way you'd want a parent like me to see him treated. He got a zero before anyone heard from him.

It's 4:20. I'll ask once more, plainly. What's the report, what's the date on it, and who decided on the zero?"
So I'd love your blessing to handle this my way. I trust your judgment, and I hope you'll trust mine.

"'Handle this my way.'" *She repeats it flatly.* "I don't know what that is. You haven't told me.

I don't give a blessing to a method I haven't seen. I've spent twenty years watching people sign off on 'trust me' and find out later what they agreed to.

So tell me what 'your way' is. What are the steps, who is involved, and what goes in Owen's file?

And whatever you say, I'll want it in an email before I leave this building."
